prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your home, budget, timing, and the installer’s skill. I can help you find highly rated local companies, but first here’s a short checklist and plan so you get a good installation and avoid common pitfalls.

What to look for in an Atlanta HVAC contractor
- Proper licensing and insurance (Georgia HVAC license, general liability). Ask to see proof.  
- NATE‑certified technicians (shows technician training).  
- Good local reviews (Google, Yelp), a solid rating with the BBB, and recent customer references.  
- Written, itemized estimate (equipment, labor, permits, disposal) with model numbers and SEER ratings.  
- They perform a Manual J load calculation (not just “one size fits all”) and match equipment size to your home.  
- Clear warranty on parts and labor, and documentation for manufacturer warranties.  
- Will pull permits and follow local code.  
- Offers energy‑efficient options and can tell you about local rebates (e.g., utility or federal efficiency incentives).  
- Financing options or payment plans if needed.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see proof?  
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation? Can I get the results with the quote?  
- What brand/model are you recommending and why? SEER rating? Estimated lifespan?  
- What’s included in the install? Changeout of ductwork, thermostats, permits, disposal?  
- What warranties do you provide (parts and labor)?  
- Can you provide 3 recent local references?  
- When can you start and how long will it take? What are payment terms?

Typical cost expectations (ballpark)
- Full central AC system replacement in Atlanta commonly ranges roughly $4,000–$12,000 depending on house size, equipment efficiency (SEER), and any ductwork/air handler work. Smaller, simpler jobs can be under $5k; high‑efficiency installations or complex duct changes can be well above $10k. Ask for several quotes.

Red flags
- Very low “too good to be true” price without details.  
- No written estimate or vague scope of work.  
- Refusal to pull permits or provide proof of insurance.  
- High‑pressure sales tactics to sign immediately.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC companies near you and compare reviews/ratings — tell me your Atlanta ZIP code.  
- Provide a sample list of specific questions you can read to the technician during the estimate.  

Which would you like to do next?
